name: ESP32-C3
description: Espressif ESP32-C3: a 32-bit RISC-V core (RV32IMC, ESP-RV) at up to 160 MHz, 400 KiB of SRAM, 384 KiB of ROM, external SPI flash behind an instruction and data cache, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE; the ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1's MCU. In progress (the RTOS boards plan, part 2): the core and its interrupt controller first.

memory.name: rom
memory.doc: Internal ROM0 and ROM1 on the instruction bus (TRM table 3.3-1): the boot ROM, chip revision v0.3, its image made by tools/importers/esprom.py (--base 0x40000000 --size 0x60000 --data-table 0x40059200:0x40059400, the ROM's copy table of its RAM variables; --word 0x4005FFFC=ets_rom_layout, ROM1's last word, the pointer ESP-IDF's ROM linker script names ets_rom_layout_p at 0x3FF1FFFC, to the ROM's ets_rom_layout, which no section of the ELF holds; --alias 0x3FF00000=0x40040000:0x20000, ROM1 as the data bus sees it, which places the ELF's .rodata.interface at 0x3FF1EE3C, the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth code's pointers and constant tables, which no segment loads) from Espressif's esp32c3_rev3_rom.elf (espressif/esp-rom-elfs 20241011, Apache-2.0: LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt; the ROM's code is Copyright (c) 2015-2022 Espressif Systems (Shanghai) Co. Ltd.). Bytes no segment of the ELF covers read as zeros

memory.doc: The ESP32-C3FN4's in-package SPI flash, an XMC XM25QH32C (RDID 20 40 16; esptool's "Embedded Flash 4MB (XMC)"), reached through SPI0 and SPI1 and read in place through the cache (core/mcu/esp32c3/nor.c)

functional.claims: Work in progress (the RTOS boards plan, part 2, steps 1 to 6). The ESP-RV core: RV32IMC with user mode and the ESP32-C3's own CSRs (TRM chapter 1): mstatus's MIE, MPIE, MPP and TW, a vectored mtvec, five-bit mcause codes, the performance counter (mpcer, mpcmr, mpccr, also reached at 0x800-0x802 where the ROM starts it), the trigger module's eight triggers (exact and NAPOT match on execute, load and store, tcontrol), 16 PMP entries without static priority, and the cpu_gpio CSRs. The interrupt matrix and controller: 62 sources mapped onto CPU interrupts 1-31, level and edge types, priorities 1-15, the threshold, the 4-cycle latency, the clear toggle. The boot: Espressif's own boot ROM (esp32c3_rev3_rom.elf, chip revision v0.3) runs from the reset vector, reads the strapping pins (GPIO_STRAP), reports the reset cause (RTC_CNTL), loads an ESP image's segments from the flash through SPI1, checks its checksum and SHA-256 on the SHA accelerator and jumps to it. The in-package 4 MB flash, an XMC XM25QH32C as its datasheet has it (its instructions, status registers, busy times, security registers and power-down), behind SPI0 and SPI1; the cache and MMU mapping its 64 KB pages on the instruction and data buses. UART0 and UART1 (FIFOs, frames at the baud rate, interrupts); RTC_CNTL's reset causes, RTC timer, RTC watchdog with its flash-boot protection and the software resets; the Debug Assistant's PC logging (the ROM's Saved PC). The clocks and timers: SYSTEM's CPU clock (XTAL_CLK / 2 out of reset, the PLL's 80 or 160 MHz, RC_FAST_CLK), APB_CLK, the peripherals' clock enables and resets and the software interrupts; the system timer (two 52-bit counters at 16 MHz, three comparators in target or period mode); the timer groups' T0 (prescaler, up or down, alarm, auto-reload), MWDT (four stages, write key, flash-boot protection: a blank chip resets with TG0WDT_SYS_RST) and RTC_SLOW_CLK calibration; the eFuse controller with the chip's factory bits (revision v0.3, QFN32, 4 MB XMC flash in the package, a MAC). The pins: the GPIO matrix and IO MUX (each pad's reset configuration from TRM table 5.12-1, the matrix's output signals and the IO MUX functions, open drain, input selection, the five interrupt types on the CPU and NMI sources, the strapping latch, the UARTs on whichever pins the matrix gives them); USB Serial/JTAG's CDC-ACM registers with no host on its pins (the 64-byte buffer flushed and never read, its interrupts). What ESP-IDF's start reaches beyond the TRM: the internal I2C master to the analog blocks as the ROM's regi2c routines drive it, RND_DATA's random numbers, the ROM's ets_rom_layout_p, the RTC_SLOW_CLK periodic calibration running from reset, a CPU reset clearing the permission control (TRM 14.8). The radio's register blocks as ESP-IDF's closed PHY and Wi-Fi libraries drive them (FE2, FE, the receive gain table, the AGC and NRX, the baseband, the Wi-Fi MAC's registers), their PHY calibrations answering as an ideal radio (the BBPLL and RF PLL calibrated and locked, the power detector's, DC and IQ measurements done), so that ESP-IDF's Wi-Fi driver initialises, calibrates and stores its calibration, starts the station and scans, as on a board with nothing on the air. ESP-IDF v5.4's hello_world runs unmodified, from the ROM through the second-stage bootloader to app_main and esp_restart. The peripherals on the pins (step 5): the GPIO matrix carries any modelled peripheral's output signal and gives its inputs back; RMT's two transmitters and two receivers over the 192-word RAM (normal, wrap and continuous modes, loop counts, the carrier, simultaneous start, the receivers' idle threshold, filter, demodulation and wrap, CONF_UPDATE); LEDC's four timers and six generators (the fractional divider, HPOINT and duty with dithering, fading, the overflow counter, PARA_UP at the overflow); the I2C controller as master (the command list, its timing registers' bus timing, stretching, arbitration, the timeout, the clear pulses) and slave (7- and 10-bit addresses, the general call, double addressing, ACK control, stretching), with its FIFOs; GP-SPI2 as a master (CS setup and hold, command, address, dummy and data phases on 1, 2 or 4 lines or QPI, full and half duplex, the four clock modes, bit orders, its buffer or the GDMA); the GDMA's three transmit and three receive channels on descriptor lists, memory to memory included; the SAR ADCs (one-time sampling and the timer's pattern-table scanning into the GDMA, filters, threshold monitors, attenuation, the self-calibration's grounded input) and the temperature sensor reading the world's temperature. Every register of Espressif's SVD with its reset value, and the RAMs it leaves out (RMT, I2C).
omissions: every peripheral not named in the claims: TWAI, I2S, UHCI, AES, RSA, HMAC, the digital signature and the permission control's checks (their registers keep what is written); the PLL's power and lock, and the RC oscillators' spread (they run at their nominal frequencies)
a USB host on GPIO18 and GPIO19 (the CDC-ACM port on the computer, its DTR and RTS resets, the JTAG side: ADR-031's native USB); the USB pads' own pull-ups and pin swap beyond the IO MUX's reset

the analog blocks' registers' reset values (they read 0 until written) and what their values do (the PLL's frequency comes from SYSTEM, the regulators' voltages are not modelled); the o-code calibration's time
the random number generator's entropy: RND_DATA is a seeded generator, the same sequence every run so that a run replays, whatever noise sources are on
the GPIO's input filter and synchronisation, sleep mode (the pads' sleep configuration), the sigma-delta modulation and the drive strengths' effect

RMT: the free-running divider's phase (REF_CNT_RST; each transmission is timed from its start) and the carrier's phase (it restarts with each stretch it modulates); the memory's power-down; the status registers' STATE and APB-side error bits
LEDC: a fractional divider's alternating A and A + 1 counts (each count is the average length); a CLK_DIV below 1 (the timer stops); light-sleep

I2C: the SCL and SDA filters (the nets are clean); the state machines' own timeouts (SCL_ST_TO, SCL_MAIN_ST_TO); SR's state fields; a slave's SDA_SAMPLE point (it reacts at the edge), SLV_TX_AUTO_START_EN 0 and 10-bit addressing's R/W check
GP-SPI2: slave mode and the configurable segmented transfer (USR_CONF); the timing compensation (DIN_MODE, DIN_NUM, DOUT_MODE); CLK_MODE's clock after CS; SPI_UPDATE takes no time; the AFIFO errors
GDMA: bytes move at once, with no FIFO and no bus bandwidth (the priorities change nothing); the in-link's auto return; err_eof (UHCI0's)

SAR ADC: the TRM's ideal transfer (no offset, gain error, nonlinearity or noise; the eFuses hold no calibration); ADC2's errata; the arbiter's priorities; the initial code's offset. Temperature sensor: no self-heating or settling
the eFuses' write and read protection, their check values and times; the chip's calibration data (BLOCK2 is blank)
the cache's enable and bus-shut bits, the MMU entry fault and the access counters; the cache holds whole pages, not 16 KB of lines (core/mcu/esp32c3/cache.c)
the flash's QPI mode, continuous read mode, SFDP table and block protection; SPI_MEM's auto-suspend and wait-idle, and the SPI clock's time (transfers take none)
the SHA accelerator's DMA mode and its block time
the debug module and the debug CSRs
the performance counter's load and jump hazard events
the interrupt controller's transient state after a register write

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE on the air (docs/engineering/c3-radios.md, steps 3 to 6): the Wi-Fi MAC's registers keep what is written but it sends and receives no frame, so a scan finds nothing and no network is joined; the Bluetooth blocks are not modelled. The PHY's measurements read as a calibrated front end at once (their real readings and times are not published), and the radio's register blocks' reset values are unknown (they read 0)

timed.claims: Instruction timing estimated from the RISC-V core's per-class cost table, not the ESP-RV pipeline's.
omissions: the ESP-RV pipeline's hazards
cache misses and flash latency
the SPI flash transfers' time (the flash's own program and erase times are counted)

electrical.claims: GPIO pin-model defaults at 3.3 V from the datasheet's DC characteristics (table 5-4): VIH 0.75 VDD, VIL 0.25 VDD, VOH 0.8 VDD, VOL 0.1 VDD, 45 kOhm pulls, 40 mA source and 28 mA sink at the strongest drive.
omissions: the four drive strengths (FUN_DRV)
the RTC and SPI pads' own supplies
